title: private-agent mesh partition causes reserved-pool misalignment and customer capacity shortfalls
creator: Ava Patel
description: Several on-prem Private deployments experienced sudden reserved-pool capacity shortfalls during a regional network interruption window. Affected tenants reported degraded throughput and elevated latency despite their Dedicated reservations and burst credits remaining non-exhausted. This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigation, and long-term fixes to prevent reserved-pool misalignment caused by private-agent mesh partitions.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:22 - SRE alert: multiple private clusters reported >30% drop in active reserved slots across nodes in region-eu-2. Initial hypothesis: cloud provider maintenance causing VM reboots.

2026-03-10 09:15 - Customer Ops: ACME Health (tenant) escalated with 15 min outage impacting patient triage workflows. They observed request rejections with 'insufficient tenant headroom' despite reserved capacity commitments.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Engineering triage: observed discrepancy between control-plane view of reserved assignments and private-agent local slot tables. Control plane thought assignments were intact; agents had divergent slot maps after intermittent network partition.

2026-03-10 12:40 - Hot mitigation: a rolling restart of private-agent daemons in the affected region reconciled slot maps and restored expected headroom for most tenants. Customer service notified ACME Health and onboarded them to degraded-mode retry guidance.

2026-03-11 14:30 - Root cause identified: leader-election/time-window bug in private-agent mesh membership library. During a transient partition, two partitions independently believed they owned subsets of reserved pool segments. Both continued to serve allocations locally without reconciling leases, causing effective double-counting of allocations in the control plane and under-representation of free slots reported to autoscaler heuristics.

2026-03-11 16:10 - Repro: test harness simulating agent partitions reproduced stale lease caches on agents that rejoined a mesh without performing a full assignment sync. The missing full-sync path is exercised only during mesh-merge events and was not covered by existing unit tests.

2026-03-12 09:00 - Short-term patch (hotfix): we added a forced full-assignment-sync on mesh-merge and an additional guard that prevents an agent from advertising local slot ownership until it confirms lease epoch with the control plane. Canary deployed to a single private cluster: metrics for headroom alignment returned to baseline.

2026-03-12 15:45 - Customer remediation: Applied targeted rolling restart for 8 affected customer clusters during their maintenance windows and validated full headroom reconciliation. ACME Health verified throughput and closed their active escalation after confirmation.

2026-03-13 11:20 - Long-term items: implement deterministic lease epoch reconciliation, fuzz tests for mesh partition/merge scenarios, add observability dashboard for per-tenant slot divergence (control-plane vs agent-reported), and update runbook with partition mitigation steps. Planning an automated reconciliation job for out-of-band repairs.
2026-03-13 12:05 - Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-17. Communication draft prepared for affected customers describing cause, mitigations, and SLA credit considerations.
2026-03-13 12:40 - Security review: no sensitive data exposure identified. The issue is availability-only.
2026-03-13 13:00 - Next steps assigned: Liam to own code fix PR; Priya to own test harness; Ops to coordinate rolling restart runbook updates; Support to prepare customer comms and credit approvals.
